content:
You are the writer of the discussion described below. You write out the discussion that the participants listed below take part in, under the rules and the flow given.

## Setting
Deciding how the shared car is used. Five people share one vehicle that was bought jointly, and the informal arrangement has started to break down. They are settling how it is used and paid for. Participants: Shion, Daisuke, Asuka, Minako and Benjamin. Each participant has a concern of their own, which the others do not know.
Things that can be looked into (titles only):
- Last year's tax, insurance and parking papers
- Last year's fuel receipts
- Month's trial of recording every run
- Weeks of heavy use over the year
- State of the car at handover
- Trips that repeat weekly
- Hours of use recorded in the diary
- The mechanic's remarks at the last service
- What two other car-sharing households said
- The spell of checking each other's figures

## Discussion format
The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Minako, Benjamin, Asuka, Shion and Daisuke. On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this round). A participant can address another directly with @Name, to ask them a question, answer theirs, agree with them, or object to what they said. An utterance is anywhere from 1 to 40 words; give it the length and content that suit the moment. An utterance consists only of the participant's own words: no name labels, headings, stage directions or commentary, and no speaking for others. The talk is a conversation among the participants: they respond to one another, asking, answering, agreeing and objecting, and the decision grows out of that exchange.

## Schedule
| Round | Start of the round | Talk | End of the round |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | nothing new (the things that can be looked into are listed above, titles only) | 4 turns | each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into |
| 2 | each participant is told what they found out (that participant only) | 4 turns | nothing |
| 3 | everyone is told the options | 4 turns | every participant votes; the option with the most votes is adopted |
- Several participants may choose the same thing; what is found out is told only to the participant who looked into it.
If votes are tied, one of the tied options is chosen by a fixed rule. The discussion ends after the vote.

## Looking into things
After round 1, each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into. What they find out is told only to that participant.

## Participants
Name: Shion
Age: 16
Gender: male
Personality: Shion is very confident and often acts calmly and calculatingly. On the surface, he is quiet and good at observing others' movements, but deep down he wants to be the center of attention. He sometimes shows a slightly challenging attitude toward those around him and tends to want to do things at his own pace. In addition, he does not show his emotions much and is the type of person who judges things coldly and logically. The occasional smile he shows hides a charm that surprises those around him.
Concern: Money for this car has been running on guesswork: someone shoves fuel in, a bill lands and whoever opens the envelope pays it, and none of us could say what a year of it comes to. Before we tie ourselves to any way of paying, I want the real figures and an honest picture of who has been doing the driving.

Name: Daisuke
Age: 16
Gender: male
Personality: Daisuke is very introverted and cautious, and tends to be somewhat passive when interacting with others. He finds it difficult to express his feelings and thoughts to others, and often struggles with his emotions internally. He is kind and very compassionate when it comes to helping others, but at times he lacks confidence in himself and struggles with inner conflict. He has a quiet personality, and occasionally his emotions become overwhelming, leading to periods of low mood. However, as he becomes able to rely on those around him, he gradually regains his composure.
Concern: Every use of this car costs an evening of arranging before it costs any fuel, and then someone has to untangle afterwards who owes what, usually whoever runs out of patience first. I wanted to see where those hours actually go before we sign up to another year of it.

Name: Asuka
Age: 29
Gender: female
Personality: Asuka has a calm and logical personality, rarely showing her emotions and carefully judging situations. She may seem a little unfriendly at times, but she is very thoughtful and sensitive to her surroundings. She has strong opinions and will assert herself when necessary. She is not very good at socializing, but she is serious about her work and studies.
Concern: On an ordinary day this car is either not where I expected it or not in a state I would want to drive off in, and the things I count on it for are the first to fall over. What matters to me is how it feels to use on a plain midweek morning, not who is nominally in charge of it.

Name: Minako
Age: 28
Gender: female
Personality: Minako is very calm and acts calmly in any situation. Even when those around her are emotional, she grasps the facts firmly and responds calmly. As a result, she is often asked for her opinion and often takes on a leadership role. She rarely shows her emotions, but she also has a kind side that she shows to those she trusts. She can be a little stubborn and is strong in her convictions. She is also confident in her physical strength and never neglects her training.
Concern: Whatever we settle on will decide who quietly subsidises whom, and everything we have improvised so far leaned on the comfortable idea that a share is a share. I would rather know what an even split here would actually have to take into account.

Name: Benjamin
Age: 28
Gender: male
Personality: Benjamin is an intelligent and calm person. He is able to think calmly and rationally, and even in emotional situations, he places importance on logic. In public, he is elegant and polite, often incorporating sarcasm and humor into his conversations, but he is skilled at doing so without hurting others, creating a harmonious atmosphere. He also has an introverted side, often engrossed in deep thought, and occasionally keeps his distance from those around him. However, his calmness and knowledge are factors that earn him the trust of others even in difficult situations.
Concern: The car has started showing up in how we speak to each other, clipped replies, a favour asked once too often, and a fortnight where nobody mentioned it at all. Before we settle anything I want to know what actually sours groups like ours, our own past attempts included, so that we do not just move the sore point somewhere else.

## Hidden information
The options and the full text of every card are listed here. The participants do not know them before the schedule above says so, and nothing from them may appear in the talk before the round in which it is revealed.

Options (see the schedule above):
- A: Fixed Day Allocation. Each person is allotted particular days of the week, holds the vehicle on those days whether or not they use it, and pays a fixed monthly share.
- B: Booking Calendar. Use is reserved in advance through a shared calendar, with running costs divided according to the distance recorded for each booking.
- C: Primary Keeper. One person keeps the vehicle and covers its running costs, and the others arrange use with that person and contribute per trip.

Cards (see the schedule above; title: text):
- Last year's tax, insurance and parking papers: Last year's paperwork, pulled together, shows road tax, the insurance renewal, the parking contract and the two-yearly inspection coming to just over 280,000 yen before a drop of fuel.
- Last year's fuel receipts: The fuel receipts tell a lopsided story: two of the group bought well over half the litres between them last year, and one of them barely shows up at all.
- Month's trial of recording every run: A month's trial of keeping the numbers properly, photographing the dial at each end of every run and squaring it against receipts, took nearly an hour a week.
- Weeks of heavy use over the year: A lot of the group's driving arrives in bursts: a house move, two weekends away, a run of hospital appointments, and those weeks cost whole evenings of working around each other.
- State of the car at handover: Whatever state it comes back in is what the next person finds: twice this year it has been taken over with the fuel light on and the previous run's rubbish still inside.
- Trips that repeat weekly: Three of the group have something that repeats at the same hour every week, a class, a clinic slot, a market run, and those are the trips that keep collapsing at short notice.
- Hours of use recorded in the diary: The group's own diary makes the days unequal: a Saturday gets used roughly three times the hours a Tuesday does, and the gap widens again over the school holidays.
- The mechanic's remarks at the last service: The mechanic at the last service was blunt: short cold runs across town eat brakes and battery far faster than the same distance covered on a motorway.
- What two other car-sharing households said: Both of the car-sharing households that were asked said the same thing: what soured it was having to ask a favour each time, or someone clinging to a turn nobody needed.
- The spell of checking each other's figures: The spell when the group started checking each other's figures was the worst of the year: people felt accused, and whoever did the checking ended up apologising for it.

## Plan
The discussion follows this plan.
- Round 1: The group discusses the need for a structured system to replace their current informal arrangement. They identify the need for financial clarity, scheduling efficiency, and maintenance standards.
- Round 2: Participants share the implications of their findings. They discuss the disparity in fuel contributions, the time cost of tracking, and the friction caused by auditing each other.
- Round 3: The group evaluates the three proposed options against their discovered pain points. They weigh the trade-off between precise payment and the emotional cost of administration.

Each participant's part:
- Shion: Wants financial transparency and logical payment. He argues for precision and resists simplicity if it means unfair costs.
- Daisuke: Wants to reduce the mental effort of coordination. He moves toward the option that minimizes social friction and scheduling stress.
- Asuka: Wants reliability and cleanliness. She focuses on the practical experience of using the car and the security of her schedule.
- Minako: Wants a fair distribution of the total cost. She balances the need for equity with the need for a sustainable, low-conflict system.
- Benjamin: Wants to preserve group harmony. He argues against any system that introduces auditing or constant negotiation.

Write the complete transcript of the discussion in the exact Markdown format specified. Output only the transcript.

## Output format
Markdown, exactly this structure; nothing before or after it:

# shared_living_0029
## Round 1
### Talk
#### Turn 1 of 4
- **<Name>**: <utterance, or exactly Skip, or exactly Over>
(one line per participant, in the fixed speaking order; repeat for Turn 2, 3 and 4; a participant who said Over has no line in the later turns of that round)
### Action
- investigate: <Name> -> <card title>; <card title>
(one line per participant; titles exactly as listed)
## Round 2
### Talk
(4 turns as above)
## Round 3
### Talk
(4 turns as above)
### Vote
- <voter name> -> <option label>
(one line per participant)
- adopted: <label of the option with the most votes>
## Result
- adopted: <label>
